To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inclusion of a xylanase in diets fed to growing pigs can improve energy utilization from diets containing corn DDGS and corn gluten feed.
the addition of exogenous enzymes to corn-based diets for nursery pigs can improve growth performance, nutrient utilization, and carcass quality.
the addition of exogenous phytase, xylanase, and protease to diets containing DDGS increased the concentration of energy in corn and 10 sources (Table 1) of DDGS fed to growing pigs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the efficiency of corn co-product utilization by pigs.
the evaluation of enzyme technologies that improve the nutritional value of energy and protein in corn and high fiber corn co- products.

the development of technologies for increasing energy concentration in corn and 10 different corn co-products (corn gluten meal, corn gluten feed, distillers dried grains with solubels [DDGS] with 30% and 45% corn oil, and 10 different sources of DDGS) fed to growing pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of exogenous enzymes in nursery diets containing corn DDGS can be used to improve the utilization of energy in nursery pigs.
the use of exogenous enzymes in corn and DDGS diets for growing pigs has been shown to improve nutrient digestibility and energy concentration, which in turn improves pig performance.
corn and corn co-products are an important source of energy in pig diets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of exogenous enzyme supplementation in nursery and finishing diets containing corn DDGS can be beneficial in improving growth performance and feed efficiency.
the addition of exogenous enzymes to diets fed to pigs can increase the digestibility and utilization of the energy in DDGS.
we have shown that the inclusion of exogenous enzymes in the nursery diet improves the digestibility of energy from high fiber corn co products (Whitney, 2008).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of enzymes in the diet can be an effective tool for increasing the digestibility of energy, amino acids, and other nutrients in corn DDGS and other high fiber co-products.
the energy in DDGS can be increased by using exogenous enzymes.

the use of exogenous enzymes can be an effective strategy to increase the energy value of DDGS and other high fiber co-products, and this can help to reduce the amount of energy and amino acids needed to be supplied in the diets.
